section_summary: This section contains Federal Bureau of Investigation correspondence and attached reports concerning Japanese nationals, alleged espionage and courier activity, and Japanese-owned businesses in wartime Bolivia. It focuses particularly on Takeshi Honda and Ricardo and Bertha Yoshizaki, while a lengthy survey describes the Sociedad Anónima Agrícola, commercial firms, economic controls, deportations, and Japanese residents throughout Bolivia. Later investigations cast doubt on the accusations that Honda was an aviator or agent and that the Yoshizakis regularly served as couriers.

subfiles.title: Soke Takesi Honda—Bolivia
subfiles.doc_type: FBI covering letter with translated documentary attachment
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon, Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State
subfiles.about: Transmits and summarizes papers seized from Takeshi Honda after Bolivian police suspected him of studying topography and conducting aerial reconnaissance.
subfiles.summary: The FBI reports Bolivian police allegations that Honda was a qualified Japanese military aviator who flew reconnaissance missions, while noting that the reports were vague and that his whereabouts were unknown. The translated papers instead consist mainly of family registers, travel permits, addresses, gift records, and personal correspondence entrusted to Honda for delivery to Japan in 1942. The letters discuss wartime conditions, family affairs, and the personal confession of Kiyoshi Yamamoto, rather than military intelligence.

subfiles.title: Ricardo Y. Yoshizaki and Bertha Terán Yoshizaki—Bolivia
subfiles.doc_type: FBI covering letter and confidential-source memorandum
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon, Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State
subfiles.about: Reports allegations that Ricardo and Bertha Yoshizaki were connected with Japanese espionage and served as couriers between Argentina and Bolivia.
subfiles.summary: FBI memorandum on Ricardo and Bertha Yoshizaki: jewelry business, Bolivian naturalization, Proclaimed List status, and a source's allegation of espionage ties, characterized as dubious.

subfiles.title: Japanese Organizations in Bolivia
subfiles.doc_type: FBI covering letter with economic-intelligence report and resident lists
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon, Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State
subfiles.about: Surveys Japanese firms, the Sociedad Anónima Agrícola, and Japanese residents and naturalized citizens throughout Bolivia.
subfiles.summary: The report describes the prewar scale of Japanese commerce in Bolivia and traces the liquidation, intervention, transfer, or continued operation of major firms under Proclaimed List and economic-defense controls. It gives a detailed history of the Sociedad Anónima Agrícola, including its organizers, capitalization, attempted land purchases, and eventual listing. Individual company profiles discuss ownership, wartime mineral purchases, alleged nationalism or espionage contacts, deportations, and asset transfers, followed by locality-based lists of Japanese residents and their occupations.

subfiles.title: Ricardo Y. Yoshizaki and Bertha Terán de Yoshizaki—Argentina and Bolivia
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon, Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State
subfiles.about: Reports a Buenos Aires investigation and interview that contradicted earlier allegations of frequent Yoshizaki courier trips to Bolivia.
subfiles.summary: Inquiries show the Yoshizakis lived in Buenos Aires over two years; Ricardo proved Bolivian citizenship, denied subversion, and attributed allegations to other Japanese in Bolivia.

subfiles.title: Soke Takeshi Honda, aliases Takeshi Iwamoto and Soke Takesi Honda—Bolivia
subfiles.doc_type: FBI follow-up covering letter and investigative report
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon, Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State
subfiles.about: Presents further investigation concluding that Takeshi Honda was neither a Japanese military pilot nor an espionage agent.
subfiles.summary: Report on Soke Takeshi Honda, arrested in La Paz in 1942: his migration, an aviation medal for a small airfield donation, and a reliable source saying he was never an aviator or agent, now farming in Trinidad.
